payload.title: Multi-search: deep research for a reporting assignment across several search and research providers
payload.description:
Ryan, 2026-11-01: "We should start thinking in terms of a new feature called 'multi-search' that leverages multiple different search providers to do deep research into a reporting assignment."

Today: one assignment runs one provider. research.tavily-deep (src/papyrus_content/tavily_deep_research.py) submits a Tavily research task, polls it, and turns the report into a research packet Message plus proposedReferences (assignments_workflow.apply_research_packet, intake_research_packet_proposals). Web search now has a provider layer (src/papyrus_content/web_search.py, #963) with Tavily, OpenAI, Perplexity, Gemini and Bedrock, but only as a fallback chain for monitors.

Shape (proposal, to confirm with Ryan):
1. Fan out. One assignment asks several providers in parallel: deep-research APIs (Tavily research, OpenAI deep research, Perplexity sonar-deep-research, Gemini deep research) and/or plain searches on queries planned from the assignment brief.
2. Merge. Canonicalise and de-duplicate sources across providers; keep per-source provenance (which providers found it, rank, snippet). Agreement across providers is a signal; a source only one provider found is not discarded.
3. Synthesise. One research packet: the claims with the sources that support each, where providers disagree, and what nobody found. Proposed References come from the merged set, each naming its providers.
4. Judge. Show per-provider contribution (unique useful sources, cost, time) on the packet so the site learns which providers earn their cost. No fixed caps: budget per assignment is a site setting.
5. Run it as a long-running job (submit, poll, finalize), resumable, with failures per provider recorded and never fatal while any provider answers.

Seam (from #963): a ResearchProvider base beside Provider with research(request) -> ResearchResult, a RESEARCH_PROVIDERS map and a WEB_RESEARCH_PROVIDERS list, reusing Provider.api_key, the failure classification and SearchChain's skip records. tavily_research.py is the first adapter to move behind it.

Open questions for Ryan:
- Which providers by default, and is cost per assignment capped by a budget or only reported?
- Deep-research APIs only, or also a planned fan-out of plain searches (cheaper, more controllable)?
- Does the packet show disagreements between providers to the editor, or only the merged view?
- Automatic on every assignment, or a mode the editor picks (research.multi)?

Phases: (1) ResearchProvider seam plus Tavily adapter moved, no behaviour change; (2) OpenAI, Perplexity and Gemini deep-research adapters; (3) multi-search runner: fan-out, merge, provenance, packet; (4) per-provider contribution report and newsroom view; (5) p.apyr.us docs page.
